item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the exact required API, uses the established multipart helper, preserves FilesOption, and covers all required error cases. A introduces expressly prohibited APIs and changes the required Upload signature.","reasons":["B implements the exact signature `Upload(ctx context.Context, fileName string, content io.Reader, opts ...FilesOption) (*File, error)`; A substitutes `...UploadFileOption`.","B directly reuses `internal/multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content)`, while A adds unnecessary `NewFileWithFields` machinery.","A expressly violates scope by adding association fields and multiple public options (`WithFileDealID`, `WithFilePersonID`, etc.), which the contract prohibits.","B tests multipart field, filename, content, validation, retry, and source-reader failure. A lacks a direct Upload source-reader-error test and spends substantial coverage on out-of-contract options and retry semantics."] ,"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's request/response logic instead of routing through Add.","The public option hierarchy changes existing factory return types and expands the API unnecessarily.","The broad seekable-reader retry change alters ownership and closing semantics across RawClient, Files.Update, and other endpoints."],"risks_b":["Upload still calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing the encoded body through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add's option, decoding, and error path.","The RawClient change broadly buffers nearly every non-native reader based only on absence of WithNoRetry, even when the configured policy or HTTP method would not actually retry; this exceeds the contract and can cause unexpected memory use.","The Upload retry test verifies attempt count but does not parse and compare multipart filename/content on every retry."]}
